requirements.evidence: Every contract item is present: migration with FK cascade, nullable invited_by, unique (entity_id,email) (migration:14-29); email normalized in a model mutator (EntityInvite.php:40-45); pending scope (EntityInvite.php:66-69); sendInvite checks in the required order: authorize, validate, member check, pending check, rate limit, insert with UniqueConstraintViolationException mapped to inviteEmail, RateLimiter::hit only on success, queued mail, audit log, reset (Members.php:62-128); accept is idempotent, rejects expired invites, uses firstOrCreate, sets session and redirects (PendingInvites.php:14-63); <hr> is only rendered when invites exist (pending-invites.blade.php:2-5); modal title is ui.members_details, body shows name then email, role select has no empty option, confirmation modal uses ui.members_remove_title (members.blade.php:87-149). Gaps: the 'Members of :entity' title is not visible in the diff (members.blade.php lines 1-3 are unchanged, and only the pt_BR json key was added), so it cannot be verified; the single inviteEmail error relies on <x-input> rendering it.

conventions.evidence: Good: the new policy ability manageMembers (EntityPolicy.php:59-65), #[Validate] on inviteEmail/inviteRole (Members.php:38-42), #[Fillable] on the model, reversible down(), docs and CHANGELOG updated (docs/business-rules.md, docs/database-schema.md, CHANGELOG.md). Deviations: domain writes (invite creation in Members::sendInvite, membership creation in PendingInvites::accept, role change in saveRole) are inline in components instead of app/Actions/* classes; invitee authorization is a hand-rolled abort_unless email check (PendingInvites.php:95-97) rather than a policy; the migration timestamp 2026_10_29_120000 looks hand-named rather than generated.

security.evidence: Every write action authorizes server-side: sendInvite/cancelInvite/openMember call authorize('manageMembers') (Members.php:64,132,146); saveRole authorizes assignRole on the membership, scoped to the entity via selectedMembership() (Members.php:162-164,240-243); cancelInvite is scoped with $this->entity->invites()->findOrFail; accept/decline resolve the invite and abort 403 unless the e-mail matches (PendingInvites.php:93-99); memberRole is validated with Rule::in; mass assignment is restricted; output uses {{ }}. Minor gap: selectedMembershipId, memberRole and confirmingRemoval are client-writable and not #[Locked]. This is mitigated by entity scoping and authorization in saveRole/removeMember.

tests.evidence: Thorough Pest coverage: InvitesTest covers the happy path, normalization, owner tamper on inviteRole, invalid input not consuming the quota, member/pending duplicates, replacement of expired invites, the simulated unique-constraint race, the 10/hour limit per entity, and employee forbidden. PendingInvitesTest covers onboarding <hr> with and without invites, the switcher, case-insensitive matching, accept/redirect/session, double-accept, the expired error, and stranger 403 on accept and decline. MembersTest covers route and component 403, single error render, a foreign membership throwing ModelNotFoundException, draft-vs-save, owner role tamper, owner immutable, last manager, and the removal modal. EntityInviteMailTest checks pt_BR and en strings. Missing: no tamper test on selectedMembershipId pointing at a foreign membership before saveRole, and no assertion on the audit logs.

simplicity.evidence: Lean overall: the duplicated manager-count query is extracted into managerCount() (Members.php:241-246) and reused by saveRole/removeMember; framework features are used directly (RateLimiter, firstOrCreate, Attribute mutator). Small extras: isPending() and inviter() relation and accepted() factory state are only partly needed; closeMember() is an extra method beyond the contract (reasonable for the modal).

readability.evidence: Clear names (inviteRateKey, selectedMembership, invitation) and brief explanatory comments on the race and the claim logic (Members.php:105-118; PendingInvites.php:34-37). Members::sendInvite is fairly long (about 65 lines) and could be split. The hard-coded 'd/m/Y' date format in members.blade.php:63 is inconsistent with the locale-aware isoFormat used in the mail.

scope.evidence: Almost everything serves the task. The navbar and dashboard members-link gating (default-page.blade.php:44-46, dashboard.blade.php:17-21) follows from the page becoming manager-only. Deleting invites on entity soft-delete (Settings.php:84) is a small related hardening that was not requested.

issues.explanation: Invite creation, invite acceptance (membership creation) and role changes are domain writes done inline in Livewire components, but the conventions require one app/Actions/* class per use case that authorizes inside.
Invitee authorization for accept/decline is a hand-rolled abort_unless email comparison instead of a policy ability, contrary to 'authorization always goes through policies/gates'.
The diff adds the 'Members of :entity' pt_BR translation and a test for it, but the title markup itself is not in the diff, so it cannot be confirmed that the page renders this title.

selectedMembershipId and confirmingRemoval are server-controlled UI state but are not #[Locked], so clients can tamper with them. The impact is limited because saveRole and removeMember re-scope and authorize.
No tamper test sets selectedMembershipId to a foreign membership before calling saveRole, and no test asserts the audit log entries for invite sent/cancelled/accepted/declined.
The round 120000 timestamp suggests the migration was hand-named rather than created with make:migration.
The invite expiry uses a hard-coded 'd/m/Y' format while the e-mail uses a locale-aware isoFormat('LL').
Deleting invites on entity soft-delete is sensible, but the task did not ask for it.

review.summary: The change replaces direct member adding with an invite flow: the entity_invites table and model, queued markdown mail, a PendingInvites component on the switcher and onboarding, and a manager-only members page with a detail modal, explicit saveRole and a confirmation modal. Almost every requirement and edge case is implemented, including the race-to-error mapping and the quota counting only successful invites, and the tests are thorough. The main deviations are domain writes done inline in components instead of app/Actions and invitee authorization done without a policy, so I would approve with requested follow-ups rather than block.
